- ISO 27001:2013 certified

- SOC 2 Type 1 and Type 2 Certified

- Certified to be GDPR compliant | | | 2 | Is Disprz compliant with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS)? | PCI DSS standards are not applicable for Disprz platform, as our platform does not capture any payment card related details. | | | 3 | Do you comply with HIPAA? | Disprz platform does not handle patient's data and hence this is not applicable to us. | | | 4 | At some point, if an enterprise customer were to decide to opt out of Disprz usage, would you give them previous learning history, private content, etc as downloadable? | The customer can download the learning history, content through the disprz portal. | | | 5 | Are security audit logging retained for 3 years? | The logs can be connected to an AWS S3 bucket to retain logs as long as required. Here at Disprz, the app logs S3 bucket was created in year 2016 and all the logs since then are retained | | | 6 | Data portability – Would the customer be able to download/transfer their data from the service provider at any point in time during the contract period? | Yes, the customer can download their data (including content) from the frontend using the disprz portal. | | | 7 | Is there any DLP solution implemented? | With the implementation of Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), we secure all possible channels of communication to prevent DLP. With AVD, access to the internet/social websites is also disabled to ensure enhanced security.
Disprz has also implemented Seqrite DLP solution (SEPS-Seqrite End Point protection) and DLP software to keep the system protected from Data Leakage and malware. | | | 8 | Logs / Audit Trails | When it comes to logs/ audit trails, Disprz is using a SIEM tool called 'Loggly' to log application events related to DB activities and API call activities. As part of information security reviews, the logs are reviewed on a need basis. In general, the logs are not shared with the customers. However, in case of an incident, we can support the investigation | | | 9 | Is MDM implemented for all mobile devices (including BYOD and BYOC devices)? | This is not applicable, as no BYOD or BYOC are permitted in accessing production systems as per our policy. | | | 10 | How will you manage the respective ssl certificate needed? | Customers can buy their own SSL certificate. Disprz will facilitate the configuration of SSL certificate for  customer's specific Disprz e-learning instance. If Customers require Disprz's support,  we can get certificates from GoDaddy, which are verifiable with CAs (Certificate Authorities). | | | 11 | Who are the data sub processors? | The third party cloud service providers - Azure and AWS are the data sub-processors. | | | 12 | How many users can concurrently use the disprz platform? | The platform (web application) has been successfully tested for a concurrency of 50,000 users. | | | 13 | What are the assurances around deleting employees data (profile included) from your system? | Upon contract expiry, the content will be moved to archive storage and the same will not be available to access via Disprz application. Archived data is normally maintained for 3 months and purged and deleted forever from Azure. On a specific request from the customer, disprz will issue a ‘deletion certificate’ to assure that the data has been deleted from the system. | | | 14 | Do you conduct background verification of all personnel before onboarding? | Disprz leverages ONGrid portal for Background Verification Checks. This covers personal identity, education, experience, criminal records etc.
Type of checks include:
EDV: Highest Education record verification (single record)
EMV: Employment record verification (single record)
CCRV: Court (criminal / civil) record verification
IDV: ID verification (Aadhaar, PAN card, DL or Voter ID)- Single record
As a practice, only those employees who clear the BGV are onboarded to Disprz. | Note: We are shortly moving to a different vendor | | 15 | Does your organization follow secure coding process? | Yes, Disprz secure application coding standards are aligned against OWASP top 10 web application security risks. All development is done by engaging FTEs only. No vendor organizations are utilized for development of code in core platform features in general, due to IP concerns. | | | 16 | What security controls are in place to protect data, application and other assets: | The following security controls are in place to protect data, application and other assets -
- Access control

- secured data protection and storage

- infosec policies and procedures to govern the security of application

- implementation of IAM solution (Azure PIM)

- Security monitoring

- Azure MS Defender and AWS Guard duty for threat detection and monitoring

- Implementation of DLP / End Point Security solution

- Usage of Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) | | | | | | --- | --- | | AICPA | American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) | | SOC 2 Type I | Evaluates the design of the security controls at a point in time | | SOC 2 Type 2 | Reviews the design and operating effectiveness of the controls over a period of 3-12 months. | | GDPR (EU) | General Data Protection Regulation
The European Data Protection Regulation is applicable as of May 25th, 2018 in all member states to harmonize data privacy laws across Europe | | SSL | SSL stands for Secure Sockets Layer, a security protocol that creates an encrypted link between a web server and a web browser | Collapse action bar View all comments Open Details Panel Open Rovo Chat Add a comment Add labels Add a reaction {"serverDuration": 59, "requestCorrelationId": "d23ead79407a433cbaec0a2ea858f968"}
